root.label: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
root.summary: A conceptual framework that draws on cognitive science and symbolic AI to organize and design general-purpose language agents using Large Language Models (LLMs) as core computation units.

historical_foundations.label: Historical Foundations
historical_foundations.summary: The theoretical lineage from symbolic manipulation to modern LLM-based agents.

production_systems.label: Production Systems
production_systems.summary: Formalisms that reduce computation to symbolic manipulation via rules.

ps_definition.label: Production System Definition
ps_definition.summary: A set of rules where each specifies a precondition and an action; if the precondition is met, the action is taken. Original forms were string rewriting systems (X Y Z -> X W Z).

markov_algorithms.label: Markov Algorithms
markov_algorithms.summary: Production systems with priority ordering used to specify algorithms; proven to be Turing complete.

cognitive_architectures_symbolic.label: Symbolic Cognitive Architectures
cognitive_architectures_symbolic.summary: Systems that mimic human cognition by instantiating perception, memory, and planning to achieve flexible, rational behaviors.

soar_architecture.label: Soar Architecture
soar_architecture.summary: A canonical cognitive architecture that uses a decision loop to match productions in long-term memory against working memory.

soar_memory.label: Soar Memory Types
soar_memory.summary: Working memory (current circumstances/goals), Procedural memory (the production system), Semantic memory (world facts), and Episodic memory (past behaviors).

soar_decision_making.label: Soar Decision Cycle
soar_decision_making.summary: A loop consisting of a proposal and evaluation phase (ranking candidate actions) followed by the implementation of the best action.

soar_learning.label: Soar Learning Mechanisms
soar_learning.summary: Includes writing to semantic/episodic memory, reinforcement learning to weight productions, and 'chunking' to write new productions into procedural memory.

llm_production_analogy.label: LLMs as Probabilistic Production Systems
llm_production_analogy.summary: The analogy that LLMs define a probability distribution over possible string completions (productions) given a prompt (precondition).

prob_prod_definition.label: Probabilistic Production Definition
prob_prod_definition.summary: If X is a prompt and Y a continuation, the LLM defines P(Yi|X), sampling a completion each time it is called.

prompt_engineering_control.label: Prompt Engineering as Control Flow
prompt_engineering_control.summary: Manipulations of the input string (few-shot, CoT) act as a sequence of productions that bias the LLM toward high-quality completions.

coala_framework.label: The CoALA Framework
coala_framework.summary: A blueprint for language agents organizing them by information storage, action space, and decision-making procedure.

coala_memory.label: Information Storage (Memory)
coala_memory.summary: Modular memory components that allow stateless LLMs to maintain internal state across interactions.

working_memory.label: Working Memory
working_memory.summary: A central hub data structure persisting across LLM calls, storing perceptual inputs, active goals, and results from reasoning/retrieval.

episodic_memory.label: Episodic Memory
episodic_memory.summary: Stores experience from earlier decision cycles, such as history event flows or game trajectories, used as bases for reasoning.

semantic_memory.label: Semantic Memory
semantic_memory.summary: Stores structured or unstructured knowledge about the world and the agent, often initialized from databases (e.g., Wikipedia).

procedural_memory.label: Procedural Memory
procedural_memory.summary: Includes implicit knowledge (LLM weights) and explicit knowledge (agent code for actions and decision-making).

coala_action_space.label: Structured Action Space
coala_action_space.summary: Divides actions into those that affect the internal state and those that interact with the external environment.

external_actions.label: External Actions (Grounding)
external_actions.summary: Procedures that execute actions in the world and process feedback into text for working memory.

physical_grounding.label: Physical Grounding
physical_grounding.summary: Processing sensory input (via VLMs) into text and using robotic planners to execute language-based commands.

dialogue_grounding.label: Dialogue Grounding
dialogue_grounding.summary: Interaction with humans or other agents for instructions, clarification, or social simulation.

digital_grounding.label: Digital Grounding
digital_grounding.summary: Interacting with APIs, websites, games, or general code execution; often packaged as 'tools'.

internal_actions.label: Internal Actions
internal_actions.summary: Actions that modify or access the agent's internal memory modules.

retrieval_action.label: Retrieval Actions
retrieval_action.summary: Reading information from long-term memories (episodic, semantic, procedural) into working memory using rule-based, sparse, or dense methods.

reasoning_action.label: Reasoning Actions
reasoning_action.summary: Using the LLM to process working memory to generate new information, summarize observations, or distill insights.

learning_action.label: Learning Actions
learning_action.summary: Writing information to long-term memory to improve future performance.

learning_episodic.label: Updating Episodic Memory
learning_episodic.summary: Storing trajectories or experiences to be used as examples for future reasoning.

learning_semantic.label: Updating Semantic Memory
learning_semantic.summary: Storing inferences drawn from experience (e.g., via reflection) as world knowledge.

learning_procedural_weights.label: Updating LLM Parameters
learning_procedural_weights.summary: Fine-tuning the LLM using supervised learning, RL from environment/human/AI feedback, or self-improvement.

learning_procedural_code.label: Updating Agent Code
learning_procedural_code.summary: Modifying prompt templates (learning to reason) or creating new code-based skills for grounding.

coala_decision_making.label: Decision-Making Procedure
coala_decision_making.summary: The top-level 'main' program that runs a repeated cycle of planning and execution.

planning_stage.label: Planning Stage
planning_stage.summary: A sub-process using reasoning and retrieval to determine the next best action.

proposal_substage.label: Proposal
proposal_substage.summary: Generating one or more action candidates using reasoning or structured simulators.

evaluation_substage.label: Evaluation
evaluation_substage.summary: Assigning values to proposed actions via heuristic rules, LLM perplexity, learned value functions, or simulated rollouts.

selection_substage.label: Selection
selection_substage.summary: Choosing the final action to execute based on values (e.g., argmax, softmax, majority vote).

execution_stage.label: Execution Stage
execution_stage.summary: Applying the selected action (grounding or learning), receiving environmental feedback, and looping back to planning.

comparative_agents.label: Comparative Agent Analysis
comparative_agents.summary: Application of CoALA to existing agents to highlight their architectural differences.

agent_saycan.label: SayCan
agent_saycan.summary: Procedural memory only; external action space only; decision-making via single-step evaluation of a fixed set of skills.

agent_react.label: ReAct
agent_react.summary: No long-term memory; action space includes internal reasoning and external grounding; decision cycle: reason -> act.

agent_voyager.label: Voyager
agent_voyager.summary: Uses procedural memory for a skill library; all four action types (grounding, reasoning, retrieval, learning); learns by adding new code skills.

agent_generative.label: Generative Agents
agent_generative.summary: Uses episodic and semantic memory; retrieval/reasoning to generate reflections; high-level daily planning.

agent_tot.label: Tree of Thoughts (ToT)
agent_tot.summary: No long-term memory; reasoning-only internal actions; deliberate decision-making using tree search (BFS/DFS).

design_insights.label: Actionable Design Insights
design_insights.summary: Guidelines for building next-generation language agents based on the CoALA framework.

modular_agents.label: Modular Agent Architecture
modular_agents.summary: Agents should be structured as modular components (Memory, Action, Agent classes) to improve compatibility and reduce technical debt.

code_llm_tradeoff.label: LLM vs. Code Trade-off
code_llm_tradeoff.summary: Code provides interpretable, deterministic rules; LLMs provide stochastic, zero-shot flexibility. Use code for generic algorithms (e.g., tree search) to complement LLMs.

structured_reasoning.label: Structured Reasoning
structured_reasoning.summary: Move beyond low-level prompt engineering toward higher-level sequences of reasoning steps and structural output parsing.

lifelong_learning.label: Lifelong Learning
lifelong_learning.summary: Combining human knowledge (semantic) with self-generated experience (episodic) and skills (procedural) for autonomous improvement.

action_space_safety.label: Action Space Safety
action_space_safety.summary: Differentiating between risky internal actions (procedural modification) and risky external actions (harmful grounding) to implement safety guards.

deliberative_planning.label: Deliberative Planning
deliberative_planning.summary: Implementing propose-evaluate-select loops, mixing language reasoning with code-based simulation and adaptive computation allocation.

coala_root.label: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
coala_root.summary: A conceptual framework for organizing and designing language agents by positioning the LLM as the core component of a larger cognitive architecture, drawing from symbolic AI and cognitive science.

memory_module.label: Memory Modules
memory_module.summary: The internal information storage system of the agent, divided into short-term and long-term components to persist information across stateless LLM calls.

wm_fact_1.label: Working Memory Contents
wm_fact_1.summary: Maintains active and readily available information as symbolic variables, including perceptual inputs, active knowledge (generated by reasoning or retrieved), and active goals. (Page 9)

wm_fact_2.label: Working Memory Process
wm_fact_2.summary: LLM input is synthesized from a subset of working memory (e.g., prompt templates); LLM output is parsed into variables stored back in working memory. (Page 9)

long_term_memory.label: Long-Term Memory
long_term_memory.summary: Persistent storage divided into episodic, semantic, and procedural modules.

em_fact_1.label: Episodic Memory Formats
em_fact_1.summary: Can consist of training input-output pairs, history event flows, or game trajectories from previous episodes. (Page 9)

sm_fact_1.label: Semantic Memory Sources
sm_fact_1.summary: Initialized from external databases (e.g., Wikipedia) or game manuals and facts. (Page 9)

sm_fact_2.label: Semantic Memory Updates
sm_fact_2.summary: Language agents can write new knowledge obtained from LLM reasoning into semantic memory as a form of learning. (Page 9)

pm_implicit.label: Implicit Procedural Memory
pm_implicit.summary: Knowledge stored within the LLM weights. (Page 9)

pm_explicit.label: Explicit Procedural Memory
pm_explicit.summary: Knowledge written in the agent's code, divided into procedures that implement actions and procedures that implement decision-making. (Page 9)

action_space.label: Action Space
action_space.summary: The set of all possible operations the agent can perform, divided into external grounding and internal memory interactions.

physical_env.label: Physical Environments
physical_env.summary: Involves processing visual, audio, and tactile inputs into text and using robotic planners to execute language-based commands. (Page 10)

dialogue_env.label: Dialogue Environments
dialogue_env.summary: Linguistic interactions with humans or other agents for instruction, help, clarification, or social simulation. (Page 10)

digital_env.label: Digital Environments
digital_env.summary: Interactions with games, APIs, websites, and general code execution. APIs are often packaged as 'tools'. (Page 10)

ret_fact_1.label: Retrieval Implementations
ret_fact_1.summary: Can be implemented as rule-based, sparse, or dense retrieval. (Page 10)

reas_fact_1.label: Reasoning Use Cases
reas_fact_1.summary: Used to summarize observations, analyze trajectories, or support decision-making by providing additional context for subsequent LLM calls. (Page 10)

learn_episodic.label: Updating Episodic Memory
learn_episodic.summary: Storing trajectories or experiences to be retrieved later as examples. (Page 11)

learn_semantic.label: Updating Semantic Memory
learn_semantic.summary: Reasoning about raw experiences to store resulting inferences as world knowledge. (Page 11)

learn_llm_params.label: Updating LLM Parameters
learn_llm_params.summary: Modifying implicit procedural knowledge via fine-tuning (supervised, imitation, RL, RLHF, or AI feedback). (Page 11)

learn_agent_code.label: Updating Agent Code
learn_agent_code.summary: Modifying explicit procedural memory, including reasoning (prompt templates), grounding (code-based skills), retrieval, or decision-making procedures. (Page 11)

decision_making_procedure.label: Decision Making Procedure
decision_making_procedure.summary: The top-level 'main' agent program that manages the decision cycle to select grounding or learning actions.

decision_cycle.label: Decision Cycle
decision_cycle.summary: A repeated loop consisting of a planning stage and an execution stage.

coala_components.label: CoALA Agent Components
coala_components.summary: The three distinct concepts that define an agent in the CoALA framework.

fact_coala_def.label: CoALA Definition
fact_coala_def.summary: Agents are defined over: (i) internal memory, (ii) a set of possible internal and external actions, and (iii) a decision making procedure over those actions. (Page 15)

coala_internal_actions.label: Internal Actions
coala_internal_actions.summary: Actions that modify or read from the agent's internal state.

fact_int_actions_list.label: Internal Action Types
fact_int_actions_list.summary: Internal actions consist of reasoning, retrieval, and learning. (Page 16)

coala_external_actions.label: External Actions
coala_external_actions.summary: Actions that interact with the external world.

fact_ext_actions_def.label: Grounding Actions
fact_ext_actions_def.summary: External actions are referred to as 'grounding' actions, which interface with the environment. (Page 16)

coala_action_tradeoffs.label: Action Space Tradeoffs
coala_action_tradeoffs.summary: The relationship between the size of the action space and the complexity of decision-making.

fact_action_complexity.label: Complexity Tradeoff
fact_action_complexity.summary: Larger action spaces (e.g., Voyager, Generative Agents) lead to more complex decision-making problems, often requiring customized or hand-crafted procedures. (Page 16)

fact_action_safety.label: Action Space Safety
fact_action_safety.summary: Learning actions can cause internal harm (procedural deletion), while grounding actions can cause external harm (e.g., 'rm' in bash, harmful speech). (Page 16)

coala_memory_types.label: Memory Types
coala_memory_types.summary: The specific functional categories of memory in the framework.

fact_semantic_mem.label: Semantic Memory
fact_semantic_mem.summary: Stores general knowledge, such as a set of items for sale in a retail assistant. (Page 15)

fact_episodic_mem.label: Episodic Memory
fact_episodic_mem.summary: Stores specific events or interactions, such as a customer's previous purchases. (Page 15)

fact_working_mem.label: Working Memory
fact_working_mem.summary: Used to track the current state, such as the dialogue state in a conversation. (Page 15)

coala_procedural_memory.label: Procedural Memory
coala_procedural_memory.summary: Memory regarding how to perform tasks, implemented in two distinct forms.

fact_proc_code.label: Agent Code
fact_proc_code.summary: Deterministic rules that are interpretable and extensible but brittle to stochasticity. (Page 14)

fact_proc_params.label: LLM Parameters
fact_proc_params.summary: A large, stochastic production system that is hard to interpret but offers zero-shot flexibility. (Page 14)

coala_reasoning_learning.label: Reasoning and Learning
coala_reasoning_learning.summary: The processes by which agents update their internal state and produce output.

coala_structured_reasoning.label: Structured Reasoning
coala_structured_reasoning.summary: Moving beyond simple prompt engineering to structured procedures for updating working memory.

fact_reasoning_frameworks.label: Reasoning Frameworks
fact_reasoning_frameworks.summary: Frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex define higher-level sequences of reasoning steps to reduce per-call LLM burden. (Page 15)

fact_output_parsing.label: Structured Output Parsing
fact_output_parsing.summary: Solutions like Guidance and OpenAI function calling help update working memory variables. (Page 15)

coala_learning_modes.label: Learning Modes
coala_learning_modes.summary: Methods for agents to acquire new knowledge or skills.

fact_meta_learning.label: Meta-learning
fact_meta_learning.summary: Modifying agent code to learn more effectively, such as learning better retrieval procedures. (Page 16)

fact_learning_forms.label: Other Learning Forms
fact_learning_forms.summary: Includes fine-tuning smaller models for reasoning sub-tasks and 'unlearning' by deleting unneeded memory items. (Page 16)

coala_design_principles.label: CoALA Design Principles
coala_design_principles.summary: Guidelines for implementing practical language agents.

fact_modularity.label: Modular Architecture
fact_modularity.summary: Agents should be structured and modular to consolidate technical investment, improve compatibility, and reduce technical debt in industry. (Page 14)

fact_decision_tradeoff.label: Decision-Making Tradeoff
fact_decision_tradeoff.summary: Tradeoff between performance (complex, problem-specific like Voyager) and generalization (simpler, domain-agnostic like ReAct). (Page 15)

coala_conceptual_dilemmas.label: Conceptual Dilemmas
coala_conceptual_dilemmas.summary: Open research questions regarding the boundaries and modalities of agents.

fact_llm_vlm.label: LLMs vs VLMs
fact_llm_vlm.summary: Modular approach uses separate image-to-text models; Integrated approach projects images directly into the language model representation space. (Page 17)

fact_internal_external_boundary.label: Internal vs External Boundary
fact_internal_external_boundary.summary: The boundary is determined by controllability and coupling. If a resource is controllable and tightly coupled, it is internal memory; otherwise, it is an external environment. (Page 17)

hieramas_framework.label: HieraMAS (Hierarchical Agent Collaboration)
hieramas_framework.summary: A hierarchical framework optimizing intra-node LLM mixtures and inter-node communication topology for multi-agent systems.

hieramas_architecture.label: HieraMAS Architecture
hieramas_architecture.summary: The structural organization of agents into supernodes.

hieramas_supernode.label: Supernode
hieramas_supernode.summary: A mixture-of-LLMs unit that implements a propose-synthesis structure for a specific functional role.

fact_supernode_composition.label: Supernode Composition
fact_supernode_composition.summary: A supernode consists of W proposer LLMs (generating diverse proposals) and one synthesizer LLM (aggregating proposals into a unified response). (Page 2)

fact_supernode_structure.label: Internal Connectivity
fact_supernode_structure.summary: Internally, each proposer connects directly to the synthesizer. (Page 2)

hieramas_mdp.label: HieraMAS MDP Formulation
hieramas_mdp.summary: The formalization of HieraMAS as a Markov Decision Process.

fact_mdp_state.label: MDP State
fact_mdp_state.summary: State x = {Role assignments r_i, LLM assignments m within supernodes, Adjacency matrix E, Input query Q}. (Page 2)

fact_mdp_action.label: MDP Action Space
fact_mdp_action.summary: Actions include: (1) Role selection/deactivation, (2) LLM selection/skip per position, (3) Edge selection for communication topology. (Page 2)

fact_mdp_reward.label: MDP Reward Function
fact_mdp_reward.summary: Reward R(x, a) balances task correctness U against token expenditure cost C. (Page 2)

hieramas_training.label: Two-Stage Training Algorithm
hieramas_training.summary: A decoupled training process to solve credit assignment problems.

hieramas_stage1.label: Stage 1: Supernode Optimization
hieramas_stage1.summary: Learning optimal LLM selection within supernodes using random graphs.

fact_stage1_reward.label: Multi-Level Reward
fact_stage1_reward.summary: Combines node-level reward (synthesizer output vs ground truth) and final system reward: Reff_i = alpha * Rnode_i + (1 - alpha) * Rfinal. (Page 4)

fact_skip_token.label: Skip Token Mechanism
fact_skip_token.summary: A special token that enables automatic pruning: skipping a proposer removes it; skipping a synthesizer deactivates the entire functional role. (Page 3)

hieramas_stage2.label: Stage 2: Graph Classifier Training
hieramas_stage2.summary: Learning the optimal communication topology as a holistic classification task.

fact_graph_pool.label: Graph Candidate Pool
fact_graph_pool.summary: A pre-generated pool of K random Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) with varying edge densities. (Page 3)

fact_graph_classifier.label: GCN-based Classifier
fact_graph_classifier.summary: Uses a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to score candidate graphs based on query and role embeddings. (Page 3)

hieramas_theory.label: HieraMAS Theoretical Analysis
hieramas_theory.summary: Formal proofs justifying the framework's design to solve credit assignment.

fact_theorem_masking.label: Masking Effect Theorem
fact_theorem_masking.summary: Multi-level rewards prevent the 'masking effect' where a system-level success hides the failure of an individual supernode. (Page 5)

fact_theorem_edge_error.label: Edge Credit Assignment Error
fact_theorem_edge_error.summary: Per-edge policy gradients incur an irreducible error rate Omega((1-rho)pq); holistic graph scoring reduces this to a vanishing estimation error O(1/sqrt(Nsamples)). (Page 5)

hieramas_evaluation.label: HieraMAS Evaluation
hieramas_evaluation.summary: Empirical results and analysis of the framework's performance.

fact_benchmarks.label: Evaluation Benchmarks
fact_benchmarks.summary: Tested on HumanEval++ (coding), MATH (mathematical reasoning), and MMLU-Redux (general knowledge). (Page 6)

fact_topology_patterns.label: Learned Topology Patterns
fact_topology_patterns.summary: Psychologist and Doctor roles consistently act as sink nodes; Critic and Economist roles act as source/hub nodes. (Page 6)

fact_lost_in_middle.label: Lost-in-the-Middle Phenomenon
fact_lost_in_middle.summary: Observation that increasing proposer count beyond 2 leads to performance drops because the synthesizer overlooks critical information in excessively long contexts. (Page 18)
